data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2021 the syndicate's gross claims outstanding were GBP 794.858m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows adverse prior-year development on the 2019 underwriting year of approximately GBP 14.9m (c.1.9% of opening reserves), indicating a net strengthening of reserves for pre-2020 years. Overall syndicate liabilities fell materially during 2021 largely due to the RITC transfer of 2018 and prior years to an external party which reduced gross claims outstanding by c.GBP 511.5m. Reported influences during the year include COVID-19 effects from 2020, named losses such as Hurricane Ida and civil unrest in South Africa, and the review of provisions following the FCA Business Interruption Test Case which did not require material additional provisioning.
raw_causal_phrases: Majority of this decrease is attributed to the RITC of the 2018 and prior years of account.
During 2021 we saw a decrease of claims incurred due to the impact on Covid-19 in 2020 underwriting year.
Management reviewed the Syndicate's overall provision in light of the outcome of the FCA's Business Interruption Test Case.
Other losses for which the Syndicate had large exposure during the year were Hurricane Ida (GBP 7.9m net) and civil unrest in South African (GBP 2.4m net).
The reserves are considered to remain an accurate reflection of the Syndicate's exposure with no material additional provisions arising from the outcome of the test case.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development figure derived from the gross claims development triangle (gross table) by comparing the 2019 'current estimate' to its prior diagonal (one year earlier). No explicit sentence quantifying a gross prior-year movement was found. The technical provisions reconciliation includes a large RITC of 2018 and prior which materially distorts year-on-year movements; the triangle was used despite this because the RITC specifically references 2018 and prior. Some LOB-level prior-year attributions are not explicitly stated in the report and are therefore null or low-confidence here.
